title: Randomized dependency throttling + SLO verification for graceful failover
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Introduce a controlled, randomized dependency-throttle experiment to validate SLO observability and failover behavior across multi-region routing, circuit-breaker activation, and load-shedding policies. Goal: confirm product SLOs (p95 latency and availability) and that fallback model routing + client backoff keep user-visible errors within agreed thresholds when a primary region or GPU pool degrades unpredictably.
background: Previous regional chaos runs focused on hard region failures and GPU blackholes. Those exercises proved failover plumbing but left uncertainty about partial degradations (dependency slowdowns, intermittent blackholes, and probabilistic GPU eviction) that cause long tails and trigger subtle retry storms. We need a repeatable harness that injects randomized dependent-service throttles and kernel-level GPU eviction signals to verify circuit breaker thresholds, graceful degradation, and load-shedding behavior.
success_criteria: SLO: p95 latency for text/generation routes stays below 450ms for >95% of requests during experiments (measured at edge before retries)
Availability SLO: user-visible error rate (5xx/4xx combined) remains <=0.5% across canary region and <=1.5% global during full roll run
Circuit breakers for dependency X and Y open and close within configured windows without causing cascade restarts
Fallback routing to secondary model variants is invoked with <200ms additional latency and does not exceed configured budgeted tokens
No uncontrolled retry storms detected (client retry amplification factor stays <=1.2)
Runbook steps complete and rollback plan executes within 10 minutes when abort condition met
plan: Prepare a chaos harness (chaos-nemesis) variant that supports probabilistic throttling: configurable by percentage of requests, variable latency injection distribution, and transient blackhole windows
Add an experiment tag to traffic router so we can mark canary traffic and apply experiment-only routing rules
Define three cohorts: canary (1% traffic, single region), regional (20% traffic, multi-region subset), global (100% traffic - only used for final validation if earlier cohorts pass)
Instrument telemetry queries and dashboards ahead of experiment; pre-run baseline collection for 2 hours
Run canary cohort with low-intensity randomized throttles (5-10% affected, latency +50-200ms) and verify metrics, then increment intensity and expand cohorts per matrix
Run scripts that simulate GPU pool eviction signals (preemption notification + immediate token throttle) without actually terminating instances to validate admission control and draining logic
Observe circuit breaker metrics and tweak thresholds in a controlled manner (one parameter change per run)
If abort criteria are met, trigger immediate mitigation: disable chaos-nemesis, increase admission control strictness, and failover routing to dedicated pools
Document all runs, anomaly findings, and recommended adjustments in this ticket and linked postmortem doc
experiment_matrix: Variant A - Dependency Throttle Light: 5% requests delayed; delay dist: uniform 50-150ms; duration: 15m; cohort: canary
Variant B - Dependency Throttle Medium: 20% requests delayed; delay dist: normal(mean=200ms, sigma=80ms); duration: 20m; cohort: regional
Variant C - Dependency Blackhole Pulse: 1min blackhole windows every 5 minutes targeting dep Y endpoints; cohort: regional
Variant D - GPU Eviction Signal: send simulated preemption + 30s drain delay for 10% of GPU sessions; validate KV cache salvage and admission behavior; cohort: canary
Variant E - Combined Stress: B + D concurrently for 10m; cohort: regional
Variant F - Amplified Retry Path: introduce client-side retry jitter removal to test amplification; run only if prior variants safe
telemetry_and_queries: Edge p95 / p50 / p99 latency timeseries (filter by experiment tag)
User-visible error rate (4xx/5xx) from edge logs
Circuit-breaker state transitions (open/half-open/closed) per dependency with timestamps
Retry amplification metric: server_received_requests / client_sent_requests ratio
Queue depth and batch sizes inside serving runtime
GPU pool utilization and simulated eviction events timeline
Tracing spans: request -> dependency X call -> fallback path timing
runbook: Pre-checks: ensure oncall and SRE are paged for window, baseline dashboards green, GitHub PR for chaos-harness merged and deployed to canary
Start canary variant A: observe first 10 minutes for expected telemetry changes
If p95 crosses soft threshold (400ms) for >5 minutes, pause and evaluate; do not progress cohort
If user-visible error rate exceeds abort threshold (0.5% for canary) for >3 minutes, abort: disable chaos-nemesis, scale up dedicated pools, and notify product owners
During regional runs, if retry amplification factor >1.5, reduce client retries by toggling feature-flagged policy
Post-run: capture debug traces and logs for any requests hitting fallbacks; collect heap/metrics snapshots for GPU servers involved
Postmortem: write findings within 48 hours and propose concrete config changes for circuit-breaker windows, admission control thresholds, and routing fallback budgets
abort_criteria: User-visible error rate >2% for any cohort
Unrecoverable GPU process crashes observed on more than 2 nodes
Circuit breaker flapping (open/close more than 10 times in 5 minutes)
